text: An ontology turns scattered records into a shared operational reality.
textPreview: An ontology turns scattered records into a shared operational reality.

text: Palantir models objects, relationships, and actions while preserving permissions and lineage.
textPreview: Palantir models objects, relationships, and actions while preserving permissions and lineage.

text:
TALK TRACK
Explain ontology without mysticism. Different systems may refer to the same real-world person, place, asset, or event using incompatible fields. Palantir’s ontology maps those records into shared objects, relationships, and actions. That gives users a common operational picture while the platform tracks provenance, permissions, and changes. The novelty is not simply search. It is a governed semantic layer between data and decisions.

[Sources]

Present the steelman and the risk together. Palantir documents granular permissions, audit logs, lineage, and a privacy-and-civil-liberties function. text:
TALK TRACK
Gawker’s Valleywag site publicly outed Thiel in 2007. Years later, Thiel secretly funded Hulk Hogan’s privacy suit over a published sex tape. A jury awarded Hogan $140 million; Gawker filed for bankruptcy and eventually settled. Thiel framed the fight as privacy, not libel. The case can be understood both as accountability for a publisher that crossed ethical lines and as a demonstration of how private wealth can impose existential legal costs on a media institution.

textPreview: For Thiel, MAGA was a stagnation thesis—not optimism.

text:
TALK TRACK
The supplied timestamp lands at the beginning of a revealing sequence. At about 33:02, Bari Weiss asks whether Thiel feels vindicated after being early to Trump. Around 34:07, Thiel explains the deeper 2016 thesis: American society is stagnant, progress is slowing, and the intergenerational compact is breaking. Around 34:38, he calls Make America Great Again the most pessimistic slogan used by a major candidate in roughly a century, because it begins by admitting the country is no longer great. By 35:09, he says the first step is to level-set and admit where the country is. Later, around 37:13, he describes the Silicon Valley political shift as a preference cascade, with Elon Musk giving others cover around 37:46. This is the clearest evidence for the stronger claim on the previous slide: Thiel did not author MAGA, but he supplied an unusually coherent theory of what it meant.

[Sources]

name: slide-title
text: Equity aligns upside. A second passport hedges downside.
textPreview: Equity aligns upside. A second passport hedges downside.

text: Everyone wins if the company grows.
textPreview: Everyone wins if the company grows.

text: Can someone shape a country while retaining an easier exit from its failures than most citizens?
textPreview: Can someone shape a country while retaining an easier exit from its failures than most citizens?

text: That does not prove disloyalty: his companies, capital, and political project remain deeply tied to the United States.
textPreview: That does not prove disloyalty: his companies, capital, and political project remain deeply tied to the United States.

text:
TALK TRACK
Use the startup analogy carefully. Equity aligns everyone around shared upside and downside. Thiel’s New Zealand citizenship, added to his American citizenship, creates a sovereign hedge: a legal right to live somewhere else if the United States becomes unstable or unattractive. That does not establish that he wants America to fail or is indifferent to its success—his wealth, companies, relationships, and political project remain heavily American. The sharper critique is asymmetric downside: he can help shape U.S. institutions while retaining more exit capacity than the citizens who must absorb the consequences. This is an incentive and accountability argument, not proof of motive or disloyalty.
